paribhashas.effect: a suffix named = the word from its base up to the suffix — “प्रत्ययग्रहणे यस्मात्स विहितस्तदादेस्तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम्”
pratyāhāra here: stands for the sounds/endings from its first member to the marker (Kāśikā glosses it as such, e.g. सुप्-ādi/-anta)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
a 7th-case word naming the setting — “in X” (not “when X follows”)

quote.q: न च श्रितादीनां समर्थविशेषणत्वात्तदन्तविधौ श्रितान्तादिशब्दप्रकृतिकैरित्यर्थलाभा॒त्कृष्णं परमश्रित॑ इत्यत्रापि समासः स्यादिति वाच्यं, समासप्रत्ययविधौ तदन्तविधिप्रतिषेधात्

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)
a suffix named in a rule stands for the word that ENDS in that suffix (starting from what it was added to) — what ENDS in it, together with what it was added to (प्रत्ययग्रहणे … तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम्)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)
a suffix named in a rule stands for the word that ENDS in that suffix (starting from what it was added to) — what ENDS in it, together with what it was added to (प्रत्ययग्रहणे … तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम्)

paribhashas.effect: what ENDS in it, together with what it was added to (प्रत्ययग्रहणे … तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम्)
विभाषा = optional (न वेति विभाषा) — the gloss keeps the term
“तदर्थार्थबलिहितसुखरक्षितैः समर्थैः सुबन्तैः सह”

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

why.txt: it describes another word of the rule

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

left.txt: a suffix named in a rule stands for the word that ENDS in that suffix (starting from what it was added to) — सुबन्ताः: a suffix (or case ending) named → what ENDS in it, together with what it was added to (प्रत्ययग्रहणे … तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम्)

why.txt: A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

ev.q: तद्धितार्थे विषय उत्तरपदे च परतः समाहारे चाभिधेये

why.txt: विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

left.txt: a suffix named in a rule stands for the word that ENDS in that suffix (starting from what it was added to) — सुबन्तम्: a suffix (or case ending) named → what ENDS in it, together with what it was added to (प्रत्ययग्रहणे … तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम्)

why.txt: it describes another word of the rule

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. why.txt: विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. “याजकादिभिः समर्थैः सुबन्तैः सह”

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

quote.q: Why do we say 'अत् with a त्' [[1.1.70]]? This rule does not apply when it is long आ as अश्वा + वृषः = अश्वावृषौ or वृषाश्वे .

paribhashas.trigger: अत्: अ with त् after it (तपर)
paribhashas.effect: only the short अ, not its other lengths
pratyāhāra here: stands for the sounds/endings from its first member to the marker (Kāśikā glosses it as such, e.g. अच्-ādi/-anta)

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). why.txt: विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

paribhashas.effect: a suffix named = the word from its base up to the suffix — “प्रत्ययग्रहणे यस्मात्स विहितस्तदादेस्तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम्”

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

why.txt: लुक् is by definition the disappearance of a suffix, so “of the suffix” is understood

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

paribhashas.effect: The Mahābhāṣya settles which of डा/रौ/रस् replaces which प्रथमपुरुष ending by 1.1.50 (nearness of meaning: singular for singular, dual for dual, plural for plural). The Kāśikā says “यथाक्रमं डा रौ रस् इत्येत आदेशा भवन्ति

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

ev.q: डा रौ रस् इति त्रय आदेशा भवन्ति

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
when two lists have the same number of members they pair up IN ORDER (yathāsaṅkhya) — they pair up in order (यथासङ्ख्यम्)
it describes another word of the rule

no.txt: not the place (a qualifier)

left.txt: a substitute of more than one sound (or शित्) replaces the WHOLE — डा-रौ-रस: more than one sound → it replaces the WHOLE of the place

teaching_view.fin: लुट्-आदेशस्य प्रथमपुरुषस्य स्थाने डा रौ रस् आदेशाः यथासङ्ख्यम् भवति

why: स्थाने — the 6th case names what is replaced
यथासङ्ख्यम् — members paired in order
